logp.method_description: The lipophilicity of complexes were determined by the log of the octanol–water partition coefficient (Po/w) as described by Jiang et al. [36], using the shake classical method, this parameter represents the relative affinity of the compound by water and oil. First, a mixture of PBS and octanol (1:1) were kept under agitation in a shaker for 24 h. Then, the mixture rested to obtain two phases, PBS saturated with octanol, and octanol saturated with PBS. The complexes were dissolved in PBS (these solutions were named as Co), and in PBS saturated with octanol to obtain solution of 20 µmol L-1. The solutions of PBS saturated with octanol were mixed with the same volume of octanol saturated with PBS, and put in agitation for 24 h in the shaker, after this time, solutions were kept at rest for 24 h to separate the two phases. Finally, the phase of PBS was named as Cw. The octanol–water partition coefficients were determined using the following equation, Po/w = (Co - Cw)/Cw, and the concentration was determined by spectrometric method using the Lambert–Beer equation.
